sources.source_subject: fix: speed up MCP node writes
sources.behavior: fix: add :validate-changed-only? option to import-edn-data so batch imports skip full-graph validation (use import-tx-data directly) when only changed entities need checking; upsert-nodes passes {:validate-changed-only? true}
sources.upstream_evidence: main b517311813 IMPLEMENTED A SUPERSET of this behavior with a different, more general API: op.cljs import-edn-data (line 213) destructures {:keys [tx-meta validate-scope]} and passes (cond-> {:edn-label "Imported EDN"} validate-scope (assoc :validate-scope validate-scope)) to validate-import-txs; cli.cljs upsert-nodes (line 51) calls (outliner-op/batch-import-edn! edn-data {:validate-scope :tx}). The validate-import-txs docstring (deps/db/src/logseq/db/sqlite/export.cljs line 1396) explicitly states ':tx validates only entities touched by the import tx. Use :tx for incremental API/MCP writes; keep :graph for file and graph imports.' The :tx scope is a strict superset of :validate-changed-only? (which only toggled whether to call validate-import-txs at all) — it still runs validation but scoped to the tx's touched entities, which is SAFER (the spec said 'don't skip safe validation'). The source-era 'MCP skip vs validate-scope' spec is satisfied by the upstream :validate-scope :tx path. NO empty commit created; NO port (porting the obsolete :validate-changed-only? API would conflict with and be inferior to the upstream :validate-scope API). The source-era op_test.cljs tests (batch-import-edn-validates-only-changed-entities-test, batch-import-edn-validates-invalid-imported-property-test) test the :validate-changed-only? option which does not exist on main; main's equivalent coverage would go through :validate-scope :tx (not added here — out of scope, and main already ships the behavior)
sources.test: not ported (already upstream); no test run needed. Verified by reading main's final functions: op.cljs:213-228, cli.cljs:42-55, export.cljs:1330-1410 (validate-import-txs + import-tx-data)
